step1_summary: Chief complaint: New swelling over the left elbow noticed ~1 week ago.
Symptoms: Painless or minimally tender swelling; slight warmth; no significant redness; full range of motion; no systemic symptoms (fever, malaise). No clear inciting trauma. First episode.
Past medical history: Self-reported osteoarthritis diagnosed years ago. Peanut allergy. Otherwise healthy.
Medications / allergies: No regular medications. Allergic to peanuts; no known drug allergies.
Family/social history: Desk job, runs 2–3×/week. No known family rheumatologic disease. Non-contributory social history otherwise.

Vital signs / exam: No vitals provided. Video exam—visible swelling over olecranon, surrounding skin slightly warm, minimally tender adjacent to tip; overlying skin appears somewhat dry; elbow moves normally.
Labs / imaging: None yet. Plan for blood tests (CBC, inflammatory markers, rheumatologic antibodies, urate).

V: Superficial venous thrombosis of elbow region: could cause localized swelling and warmth, but very uncommon at olecranon and usually painful.
I: Septic olecranon bursitis: infection of the bursa produces swelling, warmth; needs exclusion.
Aseptic (inflammatory) olecranon bursitis: non-infectious irritation/inflammation of bursa fits painless swelling without systemic signs.
N: Soft-tissue tumor (lipoma, sarcoma): painless mass possible, though acute 1-week onset less typical.
D: Elbow osteoarthritis with joint effusion: OA can cause swelling but typically involves joint line, often painful and chronic.
I2: Drug-induced edema (e.g., dihydropyridine CCBs, steroids): patient not on meds.
C: Congenital olecranon bursopathy/abnormal bursal enlargement—rare, unlikely.
A: Rheumatoid arthritis bursitis/nodule: autoimmune disorder can present with olecranon nodules or bursitis.
T: Post-traumatic bursitis / hematoma: repetitive leaning on elbows or minor unnoticed trauma may inflame the bursa.
E: Gouty bursitis (urate crystal deposition): gout can inflame olecranon bursa; must consider, especially in middle-aged men.

step3_ranked_ddx.explanation: Classic presentation: recent onset of painless, mildly warm swelling over olecranon with preserved range of motion and lack of systemic illness. No obvious trauma needed—could be minor unnoticed pressure.
supporting_evidence: Localised swelling directly over tip of elbow
Minimal pain, only mild tenderness adjacent to bursa
Slight warmth but no marked erythema or systemic signs
No trauma required—desk work may involve leaning on elbow
opposing_evidence: Warmth raises question of infection (but can occur in aseptic bursitis)

step3_ranked_ddx.explanation: Infection of the bursa can mimic aseptic bursitis; warmth present. Needs exclusion because untreated infection can progress.
supporting_evidence: Slight warmth and tenderness at swelling site
Olecranon bursa is prone to infection even without major trauma
opposing_evidence: No redness spreading, severe pain, or functional limitation

step3_ranked_ddx.explanation: Gout frequently affects the olecranon bursa causing painless to mildly painful swellings; age/sex fit. Blood urate test ordered.
supporting_evidence: Olecranon bursa common extra-articular gout site
opposing_evidence: No prior gout history, classic foot attacks, or hyperuricemia noted
Swelling described as new, not recurrent; no mention of tophi appearance

step3_ranked_ddx.explanation: Direct blow or repeated pressure can cause bleeding/inflammation of bursa, but patient denies trauma.
supporting_evidence: Desk work could still involve leaning on elbows
opposing_evidence: Rapid recognition of swelling without bruising described

step3_ranked_ddx.explanation: Could present as painless mass, but acute 1-week onset and slight warmth argue against neoplasm.
opposing_evidence: Warmth suggests inflammation rather than tumor
